78	\subsection{When Does Pruning Method Matter? CV as Sensitivity Indicator}
79	\label{sec:cv_sensitivity}
80	
81	Token importance CV (coefficient of variation of L2 norms), measured across all six architectures spanning three connector families (Table~\ref{tab:model_properties}), correlates with the retention ratio at which the choice of pruning method becomes critical. At mild pruning ($k{=}0.95$), method sensitivity is evaluated on the three closed-loop models with distinct CV values (excluding SmolVLA, whose 0.0\% SR precludes method comparison).
82	
83	For $\pi_{0.5}$ (CV$\,{=}\,$0.055), the method gap at $k{=}0.95$ is substantial: 98.2\% (L2) versus 69.4\% (random) on Object, a 28.8\,pp difference. On Spatial, the gap is 21.4\,pp (97.8\% vs.\ 76.4\%). The near-uniform token norms cause L2 norm ranking to exploit small spatial correlations rather than genuine importance differences, while random selection preserves the uniform spatial coverage these models depend on.
84	
85	For X-VLA (CV$\,{=}\,$0.151), the method gap at $k{=}0.95$ is minimal on Object (0.2\,pp; Table~\ref{tab:main_results}). Across all four suites, the method gap averages 0.8\,pp (range 0.2--1.4\,pp). The BART encoder produces tokens with a moderate importance gradient that both methods preserve at this mild pruning level.
86	
87	For OpenVLA (CV$\,{=}\,$0.215), the method gap at $k{=}0.95$ is 1.4\,pp on Object (70.6\% vs.\ 69.2\%). The MLP projector creates a clear importance hierarchy that renders both selection strategies nearly equivalent.
88	
89	The contrast is stark: $\pi_{0.5}$ exhibits a 28.8\,pp method gap where X-VLA and OpenVLA show gaps below 1.5\,pp. Low-CV models are an order of magnitude more sensitive to pruning method choice than higher-CV models at mild retention ratios. Figure~\ref{fig:method_gap} visualizes this relationship.

38	\subsection{Pruning Protocol}
39	\label{sec:pruning_protocol}
40	
41	We apply post-connector token pruning at retention ratio $k \in \{0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.85, 0.9, 0.95\}$, where $k$ denotes the fraction of $N$ vision tokens retained. Given $N$ post-connector tokens, pruning produces $\lfloor k \cdot N \rfloor$ tokens that are passed to the LLM backbone.
42	
43	Two strategies bracket expected performance:
44	
45	\textbf{L2 norm selection} ranks tokens by their L2 norm and retains the top-$k$ fraction. This importance-based strategy provides a favorable test: if a genuine importance hierarchy exists among tokens, L2 selection should outperform random baselines.
46	
47	\textbf{Random subsampling} selects $\lfloor k \cdot N \rfloor$ tokens uniformly at random. Because it ignores token content entirely, random selection provides a conservative lower bound.
48	
49	Both strategies physically remove unselected tokens and re-index position IDs to close gaps in the sequence. Pruned tokens are discarded, not replaced with zero vectors or mask tokens.
50

tool_args.old_string: Vision token pruning in VLAs is not a uniform operation: its outcome depends on the interaction between connector architecture and task complexity. Across six VLA architectures (450M--7B) and four LIBERO suites, connector coupling is the most consistent structural factor associated with pruning robustness. While backbone, encoder, and scale differences prevent causal isolation (Appendix~\ref{app:confounders}), connector architecture tracks degradation patterns across all six models. Token-independent connectors degrade proportionally to the fraction removed; token-entangling connectors exhibit task-amplified collapse. SmolVLA's pixel-shuffle produces 0.0\% SR when just 5\% of tokens are removed; X-VLA loses 1.4\,pp on Object at $k{=}0.9$ but 27.8\,pp on Goal under random pruning, a $20{\times}$ amplification. The CV of token L2 norms serves as a single-pass diagnostic that correlates with both pruning tolerance and method sensitivity across all three connector families. For architectures where all pruning strategies fail, VTR recovers a pixel-shuffle VLA from 0.0\% to over 60\% SR at 75\% compression.
tool_args.new_string: Vision token pruning in VLAs is not a uniform operation: connector coupling and task complexity jointly govern compressibility. Across six architectures (450M--7B) and four LIBERO suites, token-independent connectors degrade proportionally; token-entangling connectors exhibit task-amplified collapse, with X-VLA showing $20{\times}$ amplification from Object to Goal. While confounders prevent causal isolation (Appendix~\ref{app:confounders}), connector architecture is the most consistent structural factor tracking degradation across all six models. CV of token L2 norms partitions models into uniform, graded, and catastrophic classes without downstream evaluation. Where all hard deletion fails, learned re-encoding (VTR) recovers over 60\% SR at 75\% compression.

tool_args.old_string:
SmolVLA's pixel-shuffle connector applies $4{\times}4$ spatial folding, concatenating 16 contiguous patches into the channel dimension of a single token. This operation creates irreversible cross-token spatial dependencies: each token encodes a $4{\times}4$ receptive field, and removing any token eliminates information from all 16 constituent patches with no redundancy in the remaining tokens.

The consequence is catastrophic. SmolVLA collapses to 0.0\% SR at $k{=}0.95$ (removing 6 of 128 tokens, a 5\% reduction) across all four LIBERO suites (Object, Spatial, Goal, Long) and both pruning methods (L2 norm and random). We verified this result on two independent checkpoints: our LoRA fine-tuned reproduction (44.8\% SR baseline) and the official SmolVLA checkpoint (59.2\% SR baseline). Both exhibit identical collapse. The cliff is architectural, not a training artifact.

The pixel-shuffle mechanism explains why the collapse is method-independent. Because all tokens carry spatially entangled information from non-overlapping $4{\times}4$ grids, no scoring function can identify ``dispensable'' tokens. L2 norm ranking and random selection fail equally because the problem is not which tokens are removed but that any removal breaks the spatial completeness the downstream LLM requires. In contrast, MLP projectors (OpenVLA) and linear projections ($\pi_{0.5}$) map patches independently. Each token retains per-patch spatial locality, so partial removal does not destroy information from unrelated spatial positions.
tool_args.new_string:
SmolVLA's pixel-shuffle connector applies $4{\times}4$ spatial folding, concatenating 16 contiguous patches into each token's channel dimension. Each token encodes a non-overlapping $4{\times}4$ receptive field with no redundancy in remaining tokens. SmolVLA collapses to 0.0\% SR at $k{=}0.95$ (removing 6 of 128 tokens) across all four LIBERO suites and both pruning methods, verified on two independent checkpoints (our LoRA reproduction at 44.8\% baseline and the official checkpoint at 59.2\%). The cliff is architectural, not a training artifact.

The collapse is method-independent: all tokens carry spatially entangled information from non-overlapping grids, so no scoring function can identify dispensable tokens. The failure is not which tokens are removed but that any removal breaks the spatial completeness the LLM requires. In contrast, token-independent connectors retain per-patch locality, so partial removal does not destroy information from unrelated positions.

tool_args.old_string: Vision Token Re-encoder (VTR) addresses the catastrophic cliff through learned re-encoding rather than hard deletion. A lightweight cross-attention module ($\sim$22M parameters, ${\sim}$5\% of SmolVLA) uses $M$ learned queries to attend over all 128 source tokens. VTR recovers SmolVLA from 0.0\% to over 60\% SR at 75\% compression ($M{=}32$: 60.1 $\pm$ 1.3\%, 3 seeds), where all hard pruning methods fail. The M-curve is flat: $M{=}16$ (87.5\% compression) matches $M{=}128$ (passthrough) within 1.1\,pp, confirming that learned re-encoding, not the compression ratio, is the operative factor. A parameter-matched MLP adapter achieves comparable performance (63.4 $\pm$ 2.6\%, $p = 0.15$), indicating the gain stems from re-encoding itself. Cross-suite evaluation confirms generalization: Spatial 53.2\% and Goal 56.4\%, both recovered from 0.0\%. VTR is trained with batch size 4 on a single GPU versus the official SmolVLA's batch size 512 across 8 GPUs; the lower baseline (44.8\% vs.\ 59.2\%) reflects this difference rather than architectural limitations (Appendix~\ref{app:smart_compress_details}). Full results in Table~\ref{tab:vtr_results} (Appendix~\ref{app:vtr_full}).

\paragraph{Limitations.}
All evaluations use LIBERO simulation; we provide no sim-to-real evidence. The six architectures differ in backbone, encoder, and scale beyond the connector, preventing causal isolation. The CV--SR correlation relies on four closed-loop models, too few for a general law. Our methods are limited to L2 and random selection; attention-based scoring~\cite{chen2024fastv} may differ. VTR is validated on SmolVLA only. Most conditions use a single seed; cross-seed validation shows $\Delta \leq 5.8$\,pp (Appendix~\ref{app:pi05_multiseed},~\ref{app:openvla_multiseed}). Extended discussion in Appendix~\ref{app:discussion}.

1	\section{Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:conclusion}
3	
4	Vision token pruning in VLAs is not a uniform operation: connector coupling and task complexity jointly govern compressibility. Across six architectures (450M--7B) and four LIBERO suites, token-independent connectors degrade proportionally; token-entangling connectors exhibit task-amplified collapse, with X-VLA showing $20{\times}$ amplification from Object to Goal. While confounders prevent causal isolation (Appendix~\ref{app:confounders}), connector architecture is the most consistent structural factor tracking degradation across all six models. CV of token L2 norms partitions models into uniform, graded, and catastrophic classes without downstream evaluation. Where all hard deletion fails, learned re-encoding (VTR) recovers over 60\% SR at 75\% compression.
